clue.text: After depression, the ranch arranged new work for old man

indicators.note: something arranged anew has been set out in a fresh order, so those letters get reshuffled

parts.note: a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground
these eight letters rearranged
an opus is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: A farm labourer, after a bout of depression, finds fresh employment for an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After depression' reads as a mood, but it just places the PIT first. Pithecanthropus is the old genus name for Java Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Pithecanthropus is the early hominid fossil genus, an ancient ancestor of humans, so a very old man indeed.

clue.text: Use middle of open prison to produce a tree

indicators.note: the middle of a word means only its central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the word
the can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Advice on putting the centre of an open prison to use by growing a tree there.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a North American hickory tree grown for its nuts.

clue.text: Mayor associated with wets — sadly he was infatuated with Thatcher

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A political jibe: a mayor in league with the Tory 'wets' who was besotted with Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatcher is not the prime minister but Becky Thatcher, Tom's sweetheart in Mark Twain's novel; 'wets' was Thatcher's label for moderate Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: In Twain's The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, the hero falls for his classmate Becky Thatcher.

clue.text: Finally nibble crackers passed round with this?

definitions.text: Finally nibble crackers passed round with this?

indicators.note: something passed round is turned about, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: crackers is slang for crazy

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the following word only

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: At the end of a meal, a cheese is handed round with the crackers to nibble.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: Edam is a cheese served with crackers at the end of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a Dutch cheese, the kind of thing passed round on a board with biscuits.

clue.text: One chasing Doctor Who finally enters with robot

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so this group sits within another word

parts.note: and means together with

indicators.note: one thing chasing another comes after it in the line

parts.note: standard abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the closing letter of the word
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fan pursuing the Doctor Who cast finally gets in, alongside a robot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' reads as the TV show, but the two words do separate jobs; 'chasing' puts the one after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a robot built to look like a human being.

clue.text: Understood American historian

parts.note: tacit means implied or understood without being said
abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: Sounds like praise for an American historian whose work is easy to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was the Roman historian who wrote the Annals and the Histories.

clue.text: Celebrates runs with English folk in the Lords pavilion?

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
standard abbreviation
only MCC members may use the pavilion at Lord's

explanation.surface: A batsman's runs are cheered by the English spectators in the Lord's pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground; its pavilion is reserved for members of the MCC, the club that owns it.
explanation.definitionFit: To remember an event or person can mean to commemorate them, as on an anniversary.

clue.text: One cuts half of pack with King and Queen

indicators.note: half of a word keeps just its front portion of the letters

parts.note: the first two of its four letters
R for Rex, Latin for king
Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A card player cuts the deck and finds the king and queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' and 'pack' suggest a deck of cards, but the definition is a person or tool that pares.
explanation.definitionFit: A parer is something or someone that trims, peels or cuts away the outside of a thing.

clue.text: Tea bag — initially trendy slimming aid

indicators.note: initially says the word just before goes at the front of the build

parts.note: a sac is a pouch or bag
char is British slang for tea
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A fashionable tea bag sold as an aid to losing weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharin is an artificial sweetener used in place of sugar by dieters.

clue.text: Understanding an order

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mastery, as in a good grasp of French
second meaning: an instruction given with authority

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs comprehension with obedience, but these are two unrelated senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a thorough grasp of a subject and an authoritative instruction.

clue.text: Cotton flower placed on fancy crib

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine freely, so the letters are reimagined in a new order

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Cam flows through Cambridge
these four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A cotton flower laid as decoration on an ornate baby's cot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword river, a thing that flows; read it as a bloom and the clue stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, closely woven white linen or cotton fabric.

clue.text: Clean without water

definitions.meaning: second meaning: of a spirit, served undiluted

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a note on dry-cleaning; in fact it is a tidy word and a bar order.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means tidy, and a drink taken neat is served straight with no mixer added.

clue.text: Crush her mac in arrangement for long walk

indicators.note: putting things in an arrangement sets them out afresh, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: to rout is to defeat utterly
these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone squashes a woman's raincoat into a pack for a long hike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crush' looks like anagram fodder beside 'her mac', but it stands on its own as a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A route march is a long, steady training march by soldiers, so an extended walk.

clue.text: Agent takes in unknown graduate performers

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: James Bond, the secret agent
an algebraic unknown
Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A talent agent signs up an unheard-of group of performers just out of college.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy band is a pop group of young male singers, so a set of performers.

clue.text: Being confused, Bugs Bunny's enemy left sack outside

indicators.note: a word placed outside wraps around the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
Elmer Fudd, the hunter forever chasing Bugs Bunny, as initial and surname
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Confused, the cartoon rabbit's foe left with an empty sack.
explanation.walkthrough: The cartoon hunter appears as E. Fudd, his initial included. 'Sack' suggests a bag or dismissal, but it is slang for bed, which wraps around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Befuddled means muddled or bewildered, unable to think clearly; 'being confused' describes that state.

clue.text: King soon goes round quarry on mare

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so one word wraps the others

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
game is hunted quarry
m is a dictionary abbreviation for mare

explanation.surface: A monarch will soon ride out on his horse after his prey.
explanation.walkthrough: M for mare is a dictionary abbreviation from horse-breeding records; the word for soon wraps the rest after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the legendary king of Mycenae who led the Greeks at Troy.

clue.text: Clobber person in a sauna?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: clothing, here a knitted top
second meaning: playful, one who perspires

explanation.walkthrough: Clobber looks like a verb for hitting someone, but it is British slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a jumper, an item of clothing, and literally anyone who sweats.

clue.text: Doctor left receipts for alcohol

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: standard abbreviation
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A physician has left behind his bar receipts for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple sec is an orange-flavoured liqueur, an alcoholic drink used in cocktails.

clue.text: Rod contains anger entering ranch

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A man called Rod storms into the ranch in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod looks like a name, but it is American slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is gangster slang for a pistol, a type of handheld gun.

clue.text: Maiden on river upset sailor's rodent

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
the Usk is a river in Wales

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A young woman by the river is distressed by a sailor's pet rat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The muskrat is a large North American water rodent.

clue.text: Most of camp moving into fortress

indicators.note: moving letters around shifts them out of their original order
most of a word means all but its final letter is kept

parts.note: a base camp, shorn of its last letter
these four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops shift most of their camp inside a fort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a link word, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bastion is a projecting part of a fortification, and by extension a stronghold.

clue.text: Starbucks employee in Zanzibar is Taiwanese

indicators.note: in says the solution lies inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: found spanning the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A coffee shop worker in Zanzibar turns out to come from Taiwan.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista makes and serves coffee, the job of counter staff at a Starbucks.

clue.text: Drug dealer hides small notes in log

indicators.note: hiding something means keeping it inside, so one word holds the others

parts.note: a diary is a daily log
standard abbreviation for small
as a verb: jots down, writes

explanation.surface: A pusher conceals small banknotes in a log pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like money, but it is a verb meaning writes down.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensary is a place that hands out medicines, so humorously a dealer in drugs.

clue.text: Scottish isle contracted workers

parts.note: Staffa is the Hebridean island famous for Fingal's Cave

explanation.surface: Workers on a Scottish island have been taken on under contract.

clue.text: One leaves navigator map

parts.note: a pilot steers or navigates a vessel
Roman numeral one

clue.text: It could be perfect if stretched

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a grammatical category such as the perfect

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' reads as flawless, but here it is the grammatical perfect, one of the verb forms.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect is a verb tense, and tense also means taut, as a rope pulled tight.

clue.text: Corrupt grass

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dishonest, open to bribery
second meaning: a stiff, coarse kind of grass

explanation.walkthrough: Grass suggests an informer, fitting the crooked theme, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is slang for dishonest, and bent is also the name of a common grass genus.

clue.text: Left someone making bread for a student

parts.note: standard abbreviation
bread is slang for money, so a wage earner

explanation.surface: A baker has left his job to become a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making bread' suggests baking, but bread is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone studying a subject, a pupil or trainee.

clue.text: Cowboy gear — don't change it, young man

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction to leave text as it was
a son is a young male

explanation.surface: A father tells his boy not to alter his cowboy outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is the broad-brimmed hat worn by cowboys, part of their outfit.

clue.text: The grammarian's name for it?

parts.note: surface reading: what a grammar expert would call some object
setter's reading: the first word itself is the thing named, the word 'the' in grammar

explanation.walkthrough: 'The' looks like an article opening the sentence, but it is the thing defined; the rest says what a grammarian would call that word.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, 'the' is classed as the definite determiner, the term for that word.
